customer_question: Our product is sold under [COMPANY]'s brand (their company name appears on the product nameplate). For the Bluetooth SIG registration, should the User Name/Password (SIG login credentials) be in our representative's name, or in [COMPANY]'s representative's name? And is it acceptable for us to ask [COMPANY] for their login User Name/Password?
question_variants: Whose name should be used for SIG registration login credentials when the product is OEM/branded for another company?
Should the manufacturer or the brand owner's representative be listed as the SIG account holder?
Is it appropriate to request another company's SIG login credentials on their behalf?
actual_issue: The customer's product (a keyboard) is sold under [COMPANY]'s brand, with [COMPANY]'s company name shown on the product nameplate. The customer (the manufacturer) initially planned to register the Bluetooth SIG User Name/Password under their own representative's name, then asked whether it should instead be under [COMPANY]'s representative's name, and separately asked whether it would be acceptable for them to ask [COMPANY] for [COMPANY]'s login User Name/Password.
plain_english_explanation: Bluetooth SIG's certification rules require that registration be filed under the name of the selling company shown on the product's nameplate - in this case, that is [COMPANY], not the manufacturer (the customer). The manufacturing company is not required to register under its own name. This means the User Name/Password for the SIG registration login should be associated with [COMPANY]'s representative, not the customer's. The customer's follow-up question - whether they may approach [COMPANY] to obtain [COMPANY]'s login credentials - was raised in this thread but not directly answered; it would need to be resolved as a separate coordination matter between the customer and [COMPANY].
consultant_answer: Bluetooth SIG's certification rules require registering under the name of the selling company shown on the product's nameplate. Since this is [COMPANY]'s product, the registration must be under [COMPANY]'s name. The manufacturing company does not need to register under its own name. (The question of whether you may ask [COMPANY] for their login User Name/Password was raised but left unanswered in this thread.)
decision_logic: When a product is sold under a different company's brand (OEM/ODM arrangement), determine which company's name appears on the product nameplate - SIG registration (including the account User Name/Password) must be under that selling company's name, regardless of which company manufactures the product. If the manufacturer does not hold those credentials, obtaining them requires direct coordination with the brand-owning company - this is a business/contractual matter outside the registration rules themselves.
final_recommendation: Confirm which company's name is on the product nameplate and register Bluetooth SIG credentials under that company's representative. If the manufacturer needs access to those credentials, advise them to coordinate directly with the brand-owning company, and flag that this specific point was not resolved within this thread.
risk_if_done_wrong: Registering Bluetooth SIG credentials under the manufacturer's name instead of the nameplate brand owner's name would violate SIG certification rules and could require correcting the registration later. Failing to clarify the credential-sharing question between the manufacturer and brand owner could stall the registration process.
